task_clarity.why: A always shows the Save action plus a status pill that distinguishes loaded, unsaved, saving and failed, so 'is it saved?' is answerable at any scroll position, while B answers it only through a 'loaded' label parked next to the wrong action (Load, not Save) and gives no unsaved signal at all, though B does at least spell out the validation reason that A hides.

visual_hierarchy.why: B lets the form own the page with quiet status text beside it, whereas A puts a permanently bright filled Save button and a bordered footer bar at the loudest rank in every state, including empty and waiting where the form or the status should dominate.

density_rhythm.why: Both keep one card and spacing system, but A's footer adds a second surface whose top edge lands mid-line of the Model help text, breaking the vertical rhythm that B preserves cleanly.

state_coverage.why: A gives empty, idle, active, waiting and error visibly distinct pill treatments (notably an explicit 'unsaved changes'), whereas B renders active identically to idle and only shows 'saving...' as faint grey text, but B's error state carries the full reason while A's does not.

accessibility.why: Both show a clear blue focus ring on the Branch field and use large, generously sized buttons with labels above inputs and text-plus-colour status, but A's clipped help line and footer text over a darker bar edge closer to the 4.5:1 floor than B's plain body text.

consistency.why: A introduces a new pill component and a second footer surface on top of the existing card language, while B stays on a single button style and plain status text with no one-off treatments.

polish.why: A clips the 'provider/model or provider/model#variant' line behind its sticky footer and cuts the Model card's bottom border in all six captures, whereas B has clean edges, no clipped text and no overlap anywhere at this viewport.

empty.A: The footer makes Save and a 'not loaded' pill visible immediately, but the half-eaten Model help line at the fold makes the first screen look broken.
empty.B: Reads cleanly top to bottom with Access, Workspace, Model and the full Model help text visible, though the Save action is entirely off-screen.

idle.A: A green 'loaded' pill sitting beside Save answers 'is it saved?' at a glance, though the footer still shears the Model help text and swallows the start of Runtime.
idle.B: Green 'loaded' is clear and the form is unobstructed, but it is attached to Load rather than Save and the save action itself is below the fold.

active.A: The amber 'unsaved changes' pill is the clearest dirty signal on either set and sits exactly where Save is, leaving the focus ring to identify the changed field.
active.B: Only the blue focus ring on Branch hints that anything changed; the status still reads 'loaded', so an operator cannot tell the edit is unsaved.

waiting.A: 'saving...' appears in the footer right beside Save, the correct location, but Save keeps its full bright primary styling so the in-flight lockout is invisible.
waiting.B: 'saving...' is quiet grey text stranded in the Access card, far from the Save button, so the in-flight state reads as unrelated to saving.

long.A: The long repo URL stays on one line with no wrap or overflow and the pill still reports 'loaded', but the clipped help line and hidden Runtime section persist.
long.B: The long repo URL fits on one line without overflow and the layout stays calm, though only 'loaded' tells you this long value is committed.

error.A: A red 'save failed' pill is unmistakable, but the reason for the failure is not visible anywhere on screen and the generic restart note is the only supporting text.
error.B: The full validation message 'model must be provider/model or provider/model#variant' is shown in red, but it is stranded in the Access card far from the Model field it describes.

why: B is better at this viewport because its form reads unobstructed and its error state names the actual problem, while A's sticky footer clips a line of the Model help text in every state and reduces the validation failure to a bare 'save failed' pill. A's 'unsaved changes' pill is a real improvement in dirty-state clarity, but it does not offset the clipping and the lost error detail.
hardGateEvidence: A: the Model help line 'provider/model or provider/model#variant' is clipped by the sticky footer's top edge in all six captures.
A: the sticky footer overlaps the Model card's bottom border, leaving the card edge cut off in every state.
A: error state shows only a 'save failed' pill; the validation message that is visible in B is not visible anywhere at 900x650.
